spots.name: St John's Co-Cathedral

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: St John's Co-Cathedral is a Catholic co-cathedral in Valletta, Malta, dedicated to Saint John the Baptist. It was built by the Order of St. John between 1573 and 1578, having been commissioned by Grand Master Jean de la Cassière as the Conventual Church of Saint John.

names.ja: 聖ヨハネ准司教座聖堂

spots.name: Grandmaster's Palace
spots.summary: The Grandmaster's Palace, officially known as The Palace, is a palace in Valletta, Malta. It was built between the 16th and 18th centuries as the palace of the Grand Master of the Knights Hospitaller, who ruled Malta from 1530 to 1798, and was also known as the Magisterial Palace.

spots.name: Fort St. Angelo
spots.summary: Fort St. Angelo is a bastioned fort in Birgu, Malta, located at the centre of the Grand Harbour. It was originally built in the medieval period as a castle called the Castrum Maris.

spots.name: San Anton Palace

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: San Anton Palace is a palace in Attard, Malta, that currently serves as the official residence of the president of Malta. It was originally built in the early 17th century as a country villa for Antoine de Paule, a knight of the Order of St. John.

spots.name: Fort Saint Elmo
spots.summary: Fort Saint Elmo is a star fort in Valletta, Malta. It stands on the seaward shore of the Sciberras Peninsula that divides Marsamxett Harbour from Grand Harbour, and commands the entrances to both harbours along with Fort Tigné and Fort Ricasoli. It is best known for its role in the Great Siege of Malta in 1565.

spots.name: Auberge de Castille

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Auberge de Castille, historically in full known as the Auberge de Castille et Portugal, is an auberge in Valletta, Malta. The auberge is located at Castile Place, close to Saint James Cavalier, the Malta Stock Exchange, and the Upper Barrakka Gardens.

names.ja: カスティーリャ騎士館

spots.name: Basilica of Our Lady of Mount Carmel

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Basilica of Our Lady of Mount Carmel is a Carmelite Roman Catholic minor basilica dedicated to Our Lady of Mount Carmel, located in Valletta, Malta. It is one of the major churches of Valletta, and forms part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site which includes the entire city.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Basilica of Our Lady of Mount Carmel, Valletta

names.es: Basílica de Nuestra Señora del Monte Carmelo (Valeta)
names.it: Chiesa della Nostra Signora del Carmelo
names.ja: カルメル山の聖母教会

spots.name: Fort Ricasoli
spots.summary: Fort Ricasoli is a bastioned fort in Kalkara, Malta, which was built by the Order of Saint John between 1670 and 1698. The fort occupies a promontory known as Gallows' Point and the north shore of Rinella Bay, commanding the entrance to the Grand Harbour along with Fort Saint Elmo.

spots.name: City Gate
spots.summary: City Gate is a gate located at the entrance of Valletta, Malta. The present gate, which is the fifth one to have stood on the site, was built between 2011 and 2014 to designs of the Italian architect Renzo Piano.

spots.name: Upper Barrakka Gardens
spots.summary: The Upper Barrakka Gardens are a public garden in Valletta, Malta. Along with the Lower Barrakka Gardens in the same city, they offer a panoramic view of the Grand Harbour.

names.ja: アッパー・バラック庭園

spots.name: Fort Manoel
spots.summary: Fort Manoel is a star fort on Manoel Island in Gżira, Malta. It was built in the 18th century by the Knights Hospitaller, during the reign of Grand Master António Manoel de Vilhena, after whom it is named.

spots.name: National Museum of Archaeology
spots.summary: The National Museum of Archaeology is a Maltese archaeological museum located in Valletta, with artefacts from Maltese prehistory, Phoenician times and a notable numismatic collection. It is managed by Heritage Malta.

names.it: Museo Nazionale di Archeologia della Valletta
names.ja: マルタ国立考古学博物館
names.zh: 马耳他国家考古博物馆

spots.name: Ħal Saflieni Hypogeum
spots.summary: The Hypogeum of Ħal Saflieni is a Neolithic subterranean structure dating to the Saflieni phase in Maltese prehistory, located in Paola, Malta. It is often simply referred to as the Hypogeum, literally meaning "underground" in Greek.

names.ja: ハル・サフリエニの地下墳墓

spots.name: Collegiate Parish Church of St Paul's Shipwreck

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Collegiate Parish Church of St Paul's Shipwreck, also known as simply the Church of St Paul's Shipwreck, is a Roman Catholic parish church in Valletta, Malta. It is one of Valletta's oldest churches.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Collegiate Parish Church of St Paul's Shipwreck

names.fr: Église collégiale du naufrage de saint Paul de La Valette
names.es: Iglesia del Naufragio de San Pablo
names.it: Chiesa collegiata di San Paolo naufrago

spots.name: Republic Street
spots.summary: Republic Street, historically known as Strada Reale or Kingsway, is a principal street in the capital city of Valletta, Malta. It is about 1 kilometer long and is known for legislative, judiciary and commercial purposes. It is mostly pedestrianised.

spots.name: Tritons' Fountain
spots.summary: The Tritons' Fountain is a fountain located in Floriana, Malta. It consists of three bronze Tritons holding up a large basin, balanced on a concentric base built out of concrete and clad in 730 tons of travertine slabs. The fountain is one of Malta's most important Modernist landmarks.

spots.name: Royal Opera House
spots.summary: The Royal Opera House, also known as the Royal Theatre, was an opera house and performing arts venue in Valletta, Malta. It was designed by the English architect Edward Middleton Barry and was erected in 1866. In 1873 its interior was extensively damaged by fire but was eventually restored by 1877.

names.ja: ロイヤル・オペラ・ハウス (マルタ)

spots.name: Saluting Battery

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: The Saluting Battery is an artillery battery in Valletta, Malta. It was constructed in the 16th century by the Order of Saint John, on or near the site of an Ottoman battery from the Great Siege of Malta. The battery forms the lower tier of St.

spots.name: Our Lady of Victory Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Our Lady of Victory Church, formerly known as the Saint Anthony the Abbot Church, was the first church and building completed in Valletta, Malta.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Church of Our Lady of Victory, Valletta

names.es: Iglesia de Nuestra Señora de la Victoria

spots.name: Great Siege Monument
spots.summary: The Great Siege Monument, also known as the Monument to the Fallen of the Great Siege, is a monument commemorating the Great Siege of Malta located in Valletta, Malta. It consists of three bronze figures symbolizing Faith, Fortitude, and Civilization, standing on top of a granite base.

spots.name: St Paul's Pro-Cathedral
spots.summary: St Paul's Pro-Cathedral, officially The Pro-Cathedral and Collegiate Church of Saint Paul, is an Anglican pro-cathedral of the Diocese in Europe situated in Independence Square, Valletta, Malta. A "pro-cathedral" is a church with cathedral status though not being the main cathedral.

names.ja: サン・ポール臨時主教座聖堂

spots.name: Auberge d'Italie

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Auberge d'Italie is an auberge in Valletta, Malta. It was built in various stages in the late 16th century to house knights of the Order of Saint John from the langue of Italy, and it originally had a Mannerist design by Girolamo Cassar and several other architects.

spots.name: MUŻA

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: MUŻA is an art museum located at Auberge d'Italie in Valletta, Malta. It was formerly located at Admiralty House between 1974 and 2016, when it was known as the National Museum of Fine Arts.

names.it: Museo nazionale di belle arti della Valletta

spots.name: Auberge de Provence

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Auberge de Provence is an auberge in Valletta, Malta. It was built in the sixteenth century to house knights of the Order of Saint John from the langue of Provence. It now houses the National Museum of Archaeology.

spots.name: Tarxien Temples
spots.summary: The Ħal Tarxien Prehistoric Complex is an archaeological complex in Tarxien, within the Port region of Malta. They date to approximately 3400 BC. The site was accepted as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1992 along with the other Megalithic temples on the island of Malta.

spots.name: Church of St Catherine of Italy, Valletta

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of St Catherine of Alexandria, commonly known as the Church of St Catherine of Italy is a Roman Catholic church in Valletta, Malta. It was built by the Hospitaller Langue of Italy and it serves as the parish church of the Italian community of Malta.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Church of St Catherine of Italy, Valletta

names.de: Church of St Catherine of Italy
names.es: Iglesia de Santa Catalina de Italia

spots.name: Palazzo Ferreria

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Palazzo Ferreria, officially Palazzo Buttiġieġ-Francia, is a palace found near the entrance of Valletta, the capital city of Malta. It was built in the late 19th century.

spots.name: Castellania
spots.summary: The Castellania, also known as the Castellania Palace, is a former courthouse and prison in Valletta, Malta that currently houses the country's health ministry. It was built by the Order of St. John between 1757 and 1760, on the site of an earlier courthouse which had been built in 1572.

spots.name: Lascaris War Rooms

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: The Lascaris War Rooms are an underground complex of tunnels and chambers in Valletta, Malta that housed the War Headquarters from where the defence of the island was conducted during the Second World War. The rooms were later used by NATO and are now open to the public as a museum.

spots.name: Inquisitor's Palace
spots.summary: The Inquisitor's Palace, also known as the Sacred Palace, is a palace in Birgu, Malta. It was the seat of the Maltese Inquisition from 1574 to 1798, under the name Palazzo del Sant'Officio.

spots.name: Palazzo Parisio
spots.summary: Palazzo Parisio, sometimes known as Casa Parisio, is a palace in Valletta, Malta. It was built in the 1740s by Domenico Sceberras, and eventually passed into the hands of the Muscati and Parisio Muscati families.

spots.name: National Library of Malta

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The National Library of Malta, often known as the Bibliotheca, is a reference library in Republic Square, Valletta, Malta. It was founded by Grand Master Emmanuel de Rohan-Polduc in 1776 out of the collections of the knight Louis Guérin de Tencin.

spots.name: Basilica of St Dominic

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Basilica of St Dominic or also known as the Basilica of Our Lady of Safe Haven and St Dominic is one of the three parish churches of Valletta, Malta. It is administered by the Dominican Order whose convent is located behind the church.

names.fr: Basilique Notre-Dame des ports salvateurs et Saint-Dominique de La Valette

spots.name: St Helen's Basilica

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St Helen's Basilica is an 18th-century Roman Catholic church situated in Birkirkara, Malta. It is built on the baroque design by Salvu Borg and built by Mason Domenico Cachia. The design was inspired by, and is similar to, the Mdina Cathedral by Lorenzo Gafa.

spots.name: Is-Suq tal-Belt
spots.summary: Is-Suq tal-Belt, also known as the Covered Market, is a 19th-century market hall located in Valletta, Malta. It is notable for being the first building in Malta to be constructed mostly of iron. The building was severely damaged in World War II, and the rebuilding was insensitive to the original structure.

spots.name: Fort Rinella

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Wed, Sun

spots.summary: The Rinella Battery was a Victorian battery in Kalkara, Malta. It is commonly referred to as Fort Rinella, although it was never classified as a fort while in use. It was armed with an Armstrong 100-ton gun, which survives; the only other surviving gun is at the Napier of Magdala Battery, Gibraltar.

spots.name: Church of Our Lady of Damascus, Valletta

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of Our Lady of Damascus is a Greek Catholic Church in Valletta, in Malta, observing the Byzantine rite. It is also called Id-Damaxxena.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Church of Our Lady of Damascus, Valletta

names.de: Kirche Unserer Frau von Damaskus in Valletta

spots.name: Saint James Cavalier

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Saint James Cavalier is a 16th-century cavalier in Valletta, Malta, which was built by the Order of St John. It overlooks St James' Bastion, a large obtuse-angled bastion forming part of the Valletta Land Front.

spots.name: Manoel Theatre
spots.summary: Teatru Manoel is a theatre and important performing arts venue in Malta. The theatre is often referred to as simply "The Manoel", and is named after Grand Master of the Order of the Knights Hospitaller, Fra António Manoel de Vilhena, who ordered its construction in 1731.

spots.name: Lower Barrakka Gardens
spots.summary: The Lower Barrakka Gardens are a public garden in Valletta, Malta, twinned with the Upper Barrakka Gardens in the same city.

spots.name: Republic Square
spots.summary: Republic Square is a piazza in Valletta, Malta. The square was originally called Piazza Tesoreria or Piazza dei Cavallieri, since the treasury of the Order of Saint John was located in the square.

spots.name: Casa Rocca Piccola

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: Casa Rocca Piccola is a 16th-century palace in Malta, and home of the noble Maltese family de Piro. It is situated in Valletta, the capital city of Malta. There are daily tours from 10am till 5pm. The palace includes a BnB with 5 rooms and a restaurant called La Giara Restaurant.

spots.name: Church of the Jesuits

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of the Circumcision of Our Lord, also known as the Church of the Jesuits or the Church of the University, is one of the oldest and largest churches in Valletta, Malta.

names.fr: Église de la Circoncision de La Valette

spots.name: St Augustine Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St Augustine Church is one of the churches built during the creation of the new city of Valletta, Malta.

names.fr: Église paroissiale Sainte-Augustine de La Valette

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Collegiate church of Saint Lawrence is an old Church situated in Birgu in Malta.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Collegiate Church of Saint Lawrence, Vittoriosa

spots.name: Victoria Gate
spots.summary: Victoria Gate is a city gate in Valletta, Malta. It was built by the British in 1885, and was named after Queen Victoria. The gate is the main entrance into the city from the Grand Harbour area, which was once the busiest part of the city. The gate is located between Marina Curtain and St.

spots.name: St Francis of Assisi Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St Francis of Assisi Church, dedicated to St Francis of Assisi, in Valletta, was built in 1598 and was completed by 1607.
spots.wikipediaTitle: St Francis of Assisi Church, Valletta

names.es: Iglesia de San Francisco de Asís

spots.name: National War Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The National War Museum is a museum in Fort Saint Elmo in the city of Valletta, Malta. It is one of the most popular museums in Malta. From 1975 to 2014, its collection mainly focused on World War I and World War II.

spots.name: Auberge d'Auvergne

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Auberge d'Auvergne was an auberge in Valletta, Malta. It was built in the 16th century to house knights of the Order of Saint John from the langue of Auvergne. It became a courthouse in the 19th century, and it remained so until it was destroyed by aerial bombardment in 1941.

spots.name: Fort Saint Michael
spots.summary: Fort Saint Michael was a small fort in the land front of the city of Senglea, Malta. It was originally built in the 1552 and played a significant role in the Great Siege of Malta of 1565. Following the siege, it was rebuilt as Saint Michael Cavalier, and was completed in 1581.

spots.name: St John's Square
spots.summary: St John's Square is found in front of St John's Co-Cathedral in Valletta, the capital of Malta. It has several outdoor cafés, surrounded by a graceful arcade.

spots.name: Church of St Barbara

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of St Barbara is a Roman Catholic church situated in Valletta, Malta.

spots.name: Statue of Queen Victoria
spots.summary: A statue of Queen Victoria stands in front of the National Library of Malta in Republic Square, Valletta, Malta. Sculpted out of marble by the Sicilian artist Giuseppe Valenti, the statue depicts the Queen sitting down and wearing a shawl of Maltese lace.

spots.name: Malta Maritime Museum
spots.summary: The Malta Maritime Museum is a maritime museum in Birgu, Malta. It is housed in the former Royal Naval Bakery, which was built in the 1840s as the main bakery for the Mediterranean Fleet. The museum has a collection of over 20,000 artifacts, and it is the largest museum on the island.

spots.name: Lascaris Battery
spots.summary: Lascaris Battery, also known as Fort Lascaris or Lascaris Bastion, is an artillery battery located on the east side of Valletta, Malta. The battery was built by the British in 1854, and it is connected to the earlier St. Peter & Paul Bastion of the Valletta Land Front.

spots.name: Floriana Lines
spots.summary: The Floriana Lines are a line of fortifications in Floriana, Malta, which surround the fortifications of Valletta and form the capital city's outer defences. Construction of the lines began in 1636 and they were named after the military engineer who designed them, Pietro Paolo Floriani.

spots.name: Church of St James, Valletta

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of St James is a Roman Catholic church in Valletta, Malta. A previous Mannerist church was built on site in the early 17th century and demolished in the early 18th century to build the present baroque church.

spots.name: Admiralty House

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Admiralty House is a palace in Valletta, Malta. It was originally built between 1569 and 1570 as two private houses by Fra. Jean de Soubiran dit Arafat, a knight of the Order of St. John. The houses were later leased to various owners, including Fra.

spots.name: Turkish Military Cemetery
spots.summary: The Turkish Military Cemetery, also known as the Ottoman Military Cemetery, is a cemetery in Marsa, Malta. Commissioned by the Ottoman sultan Abdul Aziz to replace an earlier Muslim cemetery, it was constructed between 1873 and 1874.

spots.name: Mediterranean Conference Centre
spots.summary: The Mediterranean Conference Centre is a conference centre in Valletta, Malta. The building was built as a hospital in the 16th century by the Order of St. John, and it was known as the Sacra Infermeria or the Holy Infirmary.

spots.name: Fortifications of Valletta
spots.summary: The imposing defence walls and ramparts at the entrance to Valletta, built by the Knights in the late 16th century are interesting to explore.

spots.name: Rampila Restaurant and Wine bar
spots.summary: Maltese-Mediterranean fusion restaurant and wine bar in the impressive bastions. You can enjoy a fine plate of fresh seafood, meat, game, pasta or risotto there or enjoy a platter and/or dips accompanied by wine from an extensive selection.

spots.name: Malata Restaurant

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: If you are looking for a place in Valletta to have dinner on a terrace, then this is a nice place to go slightly later in the evening when the square in front of the Grand Master's palace is almost emptied of parked cars.

spots.name: Trabuxu Wine Bar

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sun

spots.summary: A charming wine bar in an ancient cellar serving light meals. It's at the beginning of a small alley parallel to Republic street, look for the wooden sign with the corkscrew. The bistro is opposite, on South Street.

spots.name: Museum Cafe

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Cosy little café with very impressive interior and amazing food. It is one of the old Maltese bars as they ought to be. Great to enjoy original Maltese ftira. The owner is super nice and accommodating.

spots.name: Croce Bonaci Caterers

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Secluded site with wery good breakfast and tremendous sandwiches. Great little café with friendly and helpful staff. Authentic Maltese food. Excellent welcome.

spots.name: Legligin

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: A set menu of Maltese dishes. Food varies each day depending on what they buy at market. Vegetarian options. No à la carte menu. Wine pairing for €40 extra.

spots.name: Old Bakery's Pizza e Pasta

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Small size pizza restaurant. Fresh ingredients for a good pizza cooked in a wood oven. The pizza is tasteful like Italian pizzas.

spots.name: Café Deux Baronnes

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Expensive even by local standards, but the cafe has a relaxed atmosphere and a good view of Grand Harbour and Fort Sant'Angelo.

spots.name: The Submarine

spots.summary: Kind and good sandwiches. The Porchetta is sublime. Most humble ftira and salads in the city. Vegan and Vegetarian friendly.

spots.name: Luciano Restaurant

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Good food for reasonable prices in a charming location near cathedral - big portions. On 3rd floor of Luciano Hotel.

spots.name: Rubino

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: Maltese traditional cuisine is served in this restaurant which was opened in 1906. Prior reservation recommended.

spots.name: Nenu the Artisan Baker

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Bakery famous for its ftira (traditional Maltese ring-formed bread). Also serves Maltese dishes and desserts.

spots.name: The Circle's Bar And Coffe Shop

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The interior is charming and the food is homely. A great air-conditioned place to have a break from the sun.

spots.name: Caffe Cordina
spots.summary: Venerable cafe, popular for lunch or for pastries & coffee in the coffee bar. Mixed reviews of the food.

spots.name: Cafe Society
spots.summary: The only queer bar in Malta. Great drinks. Guests spill out into the street in warmer months.
